# Add Memory Zeroization for Sensitive Data

## Priority: High 🔴
**Security Enhancement for v0.2.0**

## Description

Implement secure memory zeroization for all sensitive data to prevent memory disclosure attacks. This includes session keys, GSS tokens, and credential data.

## Requirements

### 1. Add `zeroize` Dependency
```toml
[dependencies]
zeroize = { version = "1.7", features = ["derive"] }
```

### 2. Implement Zeroization

#### Session Keys
```rust
use zeroize::{Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop};

#[derive(Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)]
pub struct SessionKey {
    #[zeroize(skip)]
    id: u32,
    key: Vec<u8>,
}
```

#### GSS Tokens
```rust
impl Drop for GssContext {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(ref mut ctx) = self.inner {
            // Zeroize any cached tokens
            if let Some(ref mut token) = ctx.cached_token {
                token.zeroize();
            }
        }
    }
}
```

#### Credential Cache
```rust
pub struct CredentialCache {
    #[zeroize(skip)]
    path: PathBuf,
    data: Vec<u8>, // Auto-zeroized on drop
}
```

## Affected Files

- [ ] `src/context.rs` - Context session keys
- [ ] `src/security/gss.rs` - GSS tokens and keys
- [ ] `src/config.rs` - Credential cache paths
- [ ] `src/security/mod.rs` - IOV buffers

## Testing

### Unit Tests
```rust
#[test]
fn test_session_key_zeroization() {
    let mut key = SessionKey::new(vec![0x42; 32]);
    let ptr = key.key.as_ptr();

    drop(key);

    // Verify memory was cleared
    unsafe {
        assert_eq!(*ptr, 0);
    }
}
```

### Security Verification
```bash
# Run with valgrind
valgrind --tool=memcheck --leak-check=full \
    cargo test --features zeroize

# Check core dumps don't contain keys
gdb ./target/debug/kerbsec core
(gdb) find /b 0x0, 0x7fffffff, 0x42, 0x42, 0x42
```
